senses.gloss:
āmnāya
(‘that which is committed to memory’)
------------------------------------------
The वेदस्, the basic scriptures of हिन्दुइस्म्, are known by several other names: śruti, आम्नाय and trayī. They are called ‘śruti’ since they are ‘heard’ (śru = to hear) by the disciples from the mouth of the teacher. They are ‘trayī,’ ‘a group of three’ since Ṛgveda, Yajurveda and Sāmaveda, the three earlier compilations were always considered together. They are known as ‘āmnāya’ since they are learnt by rote, committed to memory (mnā = to commit to memory, to repeat) and are handed down traditionally from the teacher to the disciple.
The word is sometimes used in the sense of कुल or lineage and saṁpradāya or tradition as also आचार or custom.
